# The positive consumer covers arbitrary finite velocity resolution, with overflow

The three radial cells are an execution case, not the full admitted output
class. This construction supplies the Gaussian masses/conditional access in
UNIFORM_QUERY_PROOF Section7 for ANY finite Cartesian grid in[-4,4]^3, plus
ONE overflow label. No additional kinetic model or stochastic sweep is used.

## 1. Positivity for every resolution

Let N>=1 be a supplied integer and split each axis[-4,4] into N equal bins.
There are N^3 interior cells plus overflow. The source/model remains radial;
the observed cells need not be radial because the density query depends on
the sampled point only through its radius.

On the cube, |v|^2<=48 and

    M(v)/M(v)^beta >=(2pi)^(-3/8)exp(-6)>D=1/3200.

Thus EVERY positive-volume subcell satisfies A_i>D B_i independently of its
width. This is not a grid finite-test argument. The overflow masses are

    A_out=1-erf(4/sqrt2)^3,
    B_out=Z_beta[1-erf(4sqrt(beta/2))^3].

Their strict A_out>D B_out is independently outward-certified. Hence the
exact positive completion applies at arbitrary FINITE N. It does not assign
the same claim to an unbounded countable grid or to continuous coordinates.

## 2. No N^3 table or target-probability oracle

Sample a proposal point Y from the KNOWN mixture density

    q(Y)=[M(Y)+D M(Y)^beta]/[1+D Z_beta],

and map it to the grid/overflow label i. That label automatically has
proposal weight (A_i+D B_i)/(1+D Z_beta). Compute only its Gaussian masses:
for an interior box, each A_i is a product of three ordinary normal-CDF
differences, and B_i is Z_beta times the corresponding beta-Gaussian product.
Their inputs are the supplied grid endpoints. Overflow uses the two displayed
constants. No dynamic f_t cell probability is supplied or estimated in a table.

Independently draw W from M^beta conditional on i; query H_t(|W|), then
accept i with the rule in UNIFORM_QUERY_PROOF. Y itself is NOT a physical
velocity output: its conditional distribution is the proposal, not f_t.
Only the label/declared quantized observation is exact.

# A subcritical hard-sphere query and positive finite-observation output

29 October2026. Consumes the full-domain radial operator certificate, not its
finite preview. This is a restricted actual-hard-sphere operation with ideal
real/random primitives. Continuous full-velocity iid output and finite-bit
implementation are NOT claimed. Signed marks are only an intermediate;
Section7 gives an actually positive normalized observation consumer.

## 1. Acquired source class

M(v)=(2pi)^(-3/2)exp(-|v|^2/2), beta=3/4. Supply a radial nonnegative f0,
its exact density evaluator, mass1, mean0, energy3 and a warranted

    ||(f0-M)/M^beta||_infinity <=D=1/3200.

The ordinary comparator receives the same density, sampler and symmetry.
One explicit source is f_delta from POSITIVE_RESIDUAL_BARRIER.md, with
delta=2^-14. Its source bound is <=5delta M(0)^(1-beta)<5/16384<D.
All source parameters and sampling are explicit; no evolved density or
norm bound is an input. Other sources must actually qualify these premises.
Initial evaluator cost is charged: uniform primitive-work claims require a
warranted uniform evaluator bound, as the explicit mixture provides. Mere
abstract computability does not give that cost for free.

## 2. Controlled mild equation

Let h=(f-M)/M^beta. Let Kc be the radial, mass/energy-controlled linear
kernel in RADIAL_OPERATOR_PROOF.md, and nu the known Maxwellian collision
frequency. The acquired coefficient is

    int |Kc(V,ds)| <=eta nu(V), eta=99/100.

Let Z_beta=int M^beta=(2pi)^(3/8)beta^(-3/2). Collision energy conservation
gives M^beta(p)M^beta(q)=M^beta(v)M^beta(w). Therefore the nonlinear term is

    N(h,h)(v)=int M^beta(w)|v-w| E_sigma
                    [h(p)h(q)-h(v)h(w)]dw.

Write nu_beta(v)=int M^beta(w)|v-w|dw. Gaussian scaling and radial convexity
give nu_beta/nu <=C_beta=Z_beta/sqrt(beta)<4. The last strict constant is a
plain rational/pi bound, not an unknown kinetic norm.

Use the mild equation with diagonal loss nu. For ||h||<=D, its nonlinear
term has norm at most2C_beta D^2 nu, and Lipschitz constant at most
4C_beta D nu. Hence the controlled map preserves the D-ball because

    eta+2C_beta D < eta+8D <1,

and is a contraction there because

    eta+4C_beta D < eta+16D=199/200.                    (U1)

These bounds hold on every time horizon, with the same constants, since
the diagonal exponential integral has mass at most1.
